chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about al-qasamah (compurgation), where did its beginning come from? He (peace be upon him) said: It was from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). When it was after the conquest of Khaybar, a man from the Ansar was left behind from his companions, so they returned seeking him and found him covered in his blood, killed. So the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, the Jews have killed our companion. He (peace be upon him) said: Let fifty men from you swear that they killed him. They said: O Messenger of Allah, how can we swear upon what we have not seen? He (peace be upon him) said: Then let the Jews swear. They said: O Messenger of Allah, who would believe the Jews? He (peace be upon him) said: I will then pay your companion's blood money.

So I said to him: How is the ruling? He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ruled regarding blood what He did not rule regarding anything from the rights of people, due to His honoring of blood. If a man were to claim upon a man ten thousand dirhams, or less than that, or more, the oath would not be for the claimant, and the oath would be upon the defendant. So when the man claims upon the people with blood that they killed him, the oath is for the claimant of the blood before the defendant. Thus, it is upon the claimant to bring fifty men who swear that so-and-so killed so-and-so, and he is handed over to them, the one against whom the oath was taken. If they wish, they may pardon him; and if they wish, they may kill him; and if they wish, they may accept the blood money.

And if they do not swear, then it is upon those against whom it was claimed that fifty of them swear: We did not kill him, nor did we know his killer. If they do that, the people of the town in which he was found among them pay his blood money; and if he was in a wilderness land, his blood money is paid from the public treasury. Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) says: The blood of a Muslim man shall not be invalidated.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْقَرْيَةِ: The people of the town; community responsibility
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةِ: Compurgation; sworn oaths by a group to identify perpetrators

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on al-qasamah and how is blood money paid if the killers are not identified?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the foundational principle of *al-qasamah* (compurgation) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the sanctity of life by prioritizing blood rights (*haqq al-dam*) over financial claims, where the burden of oath shifts to the accuser. It details the procedural mechanism where fifty witnesses swear to identify killers, with the ultimate guarantee that no Muslim's blood remains unpaid, either through the community or the state treasury (*bayt al-mal*), as affirmed by Imam Ali (peace be upon him).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the compurgation (sworn endorsements), ‘Where was its beginning?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It was from before Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. When it was after the victory of Khyber, a man from the Helpers was left behind from his companions. So they returned to seek him, and they found him covered in his blood, killed. So the Helpers came over to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so they said, ‘The Jews have killed our companion’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Let fifty men from you swear upon that it is they who killed him’. They said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! How can we swear upon what we have not seen?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘So the Jew should swear’. So they said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Who would ratify the Jew?’ So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> would then pay your companion’.

So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How is the judgement?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Judged regarding the blood what He<sup>azwj</sup> did not Judge regarding anything from the rights of the people, due to the reverence of the blood. 
If a man were to claim upon a man ten thousand Dirhams, or less than that, or more, there would not be swearing for the claimant, and the swearing was upon the defendant. So when the man claims upon a group with the blood that they killed him, the swearing would be for the claimant of the blood before the defendant. Thus, it would be upon the claimant that he comes with fifty men swearing on oath that so and so killed so and so. So he would be handed over to them, the one who has been sworn against. So if they so desire to they may excuse, and if they so desire to they may kill, and if they so desire to they accept the wergild.

And if they do not swear, so it would be upon the defendant that he should get fifty of them (the accusers) to swear, ‘We neither have killed nor do we know his killer’. So if they do that, it is the people of the town where he (the killed one) was found to be among them, should pay, and if (he was found) in the land of wilderness, his wergild would be paid from the public treasury, for Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘There would be no invalidation of the blood of a Muslim’.
